reviews.why: Implementing separate per-thread timeouts (e.g., 5000ms for stdout, 5000ms for stderr) can lead to a maximum total wait time of 10000ms if both threads hang and are joined sequentially. This makes the overall command execution less responsive and predictable compared to a single shared wall-clock deadline.
reviews.fix: Reconsider DA-001 in favor of a single shared wall-clock deadline for both reader thread joins, as proposed in DA-002, to ensure a consistent and bounded maximum total wait time.

reviews.why: `Thread.Abort` is a dangerous and unreliable mechanism for thread termination. It can lead to corrupted application state, unreleased resources, and unpredictable behavior, especially if the thread is holding locks or in a critical section. Prioritizing handle/stream closure (as suggested in DA-004 and DA-003) is a much safer and more robust approach to unblocking reader threads.
reviews.fix: Remove the proposal to use `Thread.Abort`. Rely solely on closing the read-side pipe handle or underlying read stream (DA-003) to unblock and allow reader threads to exit gracefully. If threads still do not exit after a reasonable grace period post-handle closure, consider logging the issue and moving on, rather than forcefully aborting.
